title: Clone Graph
summary: Given a reference to node 1 of a connected undirected graph, return the corresponding node in a deep copy.

contractDetails.constraints: 0–100 vertices. A nonempty input is connected with distinct labels 1 through n, no self-loops, and no repeated neighbors. The empty input is represented by a null node and requires a null return.
contractDetails.output-checking: Inspect node identity and relationships before serialization. Compare neighbor labels per vertex in any order.
contractDetails.callable: `cloneGraph` accepts and returns a node reference or null. The grid shown here is the wire representation.

statement: Given a reference to node 1 of a connected undirected graph, return the corresponding node in a deep copy. Create a new object for every vertex, copy its value, and recreate all neighbor relationships using only copied vertices. Leave the input objects and edges unchanged. The judge shows rows of neighbor labels, one row per label starting at 1. Neighbor order is free in the copy.

examples.explanation: Both new nodes point to one another.
A null reference has no graph to copy.
Each vertex is copied once even though the triangle offers two routes.

constraints: 0–100 vertices. A nonempty input is connected with distinct labels 1 through n, no self-loops, and no repeated neighbors. The empty input is represented by a null node and requires a null return.
hints: Conceptual: The same original vertex can be reached by more than one edge.
Directional: Use an original-to-copy mapping to share the correct copied object along all incoming edges.
Implementation: Create the root copy first. During BFS, allocate each neighbor's copy once, then add that copy to the current copy's neighbor list.
complexityAnalysis: O(V+E) time and O(V) auxiliary space excluding the copy, using a mapping and a work queue.
